content.title: About
content.content: Hoisin sauce is a thick, dark brown Chinese condiment made from soybeans, sugar, vinegar, garlic, and spices. It has a sweet‑salty, slightly spicy flavor with umami notes and is commonly used in marinades, glazes, and as a dip.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Traditionally produced in Jiangsu province, hoisin sauce is now popular throughout Asia and in Western restaurants.
Recipes vary: some use fermented soybeans, others incorporate black bean paste or dates.
In the United States, hoisin sauce is often used in "five‑spice" dishes and American‑style barbecue.
Vegetarian versions exist that omit fish or seafood ingredients.
Hoisin sauce is a classic accompaniment to Peking duck, roasted meats, and spring rolls.

items.title: Source of antioxidants
items.content: Sugar and soybeans contain polyphenols that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Fermented soybeans may promote a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Soybeans are rich in iron, beneficial for maintaining hemoglobin levels.

items.title: Lower sodium than regular soy sauce
items.content: Hoisin typically has less salt than standard soy sauce, which can be advantageous for sodium‑controlled diets.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Because hoisin sauce is sweet, people with diabetes or monitoring blood sugar should use it sparingly.

items.title: Soy allergy
items.content: Individuals allergic to soy should avoid the sauce.

items.title: Contains glutamate
items.content: Some versions add monosodium glutamate, which may cause sensitivity in certain people.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Use hoisin sauce as a marinade for meat, poultry, or tofu, in glazes for Peking duck, in noodle sauces, in spring rolls, or as a dip for vegetables. It can be blended with honey, soy sauce, or vinegar for a more complex flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store hoisin sauce in a tightly sealed jar in the refrigerator. Once opened, it remains good for 6–12 months. Keep it away from water to prevent spoilage.
